A gate valve is for on/off isolation. Run it fully open or fully closed. It is not made for throttling, so use a globe valve where you need to regulate flow. Pick CS WCB or forged A105 for oil, gas and process lines, SS where corrosion matters, and CI or brass for water.

Can I use a gate valve to control flow?
No. A gate valve should be fully open or fully closed. For throttling, choose a globe valve; we list them in CS, SS, CI and forged A105.

Both come from ½" to 2" with SW or NPT ends. The SS CF8M (316) body is for corrosive or clean service; the forged A105N carbon steel body is for general oil, gas and process lines.

intro: Flanged (F/T) options are C.S globe valves with WCB body in CL150 and CL300 from ½" to 12", S.S globe valves in CF8M (316), PN16 and CL150, from ½" to 6", and C.I globe valves in PN16 from ½" to 8".

Choose a globe valve when you need to throttle or regulate flow, for example on a bypass, a drain or a cooling water line. The flow turns inside the body, so a globe valve has more pressure drop than a gate valve. For plain on/off isolation, a gate or ball valve is usually the better fit.

faq: Globe valve or gate valve: which do I need?
Use a globe valve to regulate flow and a gate valve for on/off isolation. If the valve will sit part-open in service, choose a globe valve.
What does CF8M mean on the SS globe valve?
CF8M is the cast stainless grade that matches 316. Our flanged S.S globe valve in CF8M is PN16 and CL150, from ½" to 6".
Do you have a forged globe valve for socket weld?

Swing check valves suit horizontal lines with steady flow. Spring and vertical check valves close faster and can sit in vertical lines with upward flow. Wafer and dual-disk types are short and light, so they fit between flanges where space is tight, such as after a pump.

faq: Is a check valve the same as a non-return valve?
Yes. Both names mean a valve that lets flow pass one way and stops it coming back.

Which check valve should go after a pump?

faq: Should I buy a 1PC, 2PC or 3PC ball valve?

intro: We list bronze safety valves, also called pressure relief valves, with NPT connection from ½" to 2", with or without lever, in 10 bar and 20 bar. You can collect them from our counter in Al Quoz Industrial Area 3.

A safety valve opens to release pressure when a vessel or line goes above its limit, then closes again. Choose the setting to suit the equipment it protects, and never above the pressure that equipment can take. A lever lets you lift the valve by hand to check that it moves and reseats.
Brass and S.S (SS304 or SS316) air vents, 10 bar with NPT thread, in ½", ¾" and 1", are on the same page. They let trapped air out of high points in water lines.

faq: What is the difference between a safety valve and a pressure relief valve?
Buyers use both names for the same job: a valve that opens to let out excess pressure. Ours are bronze, in 10 bar and 20 bar versions.
What sizes do you have?

Do I need the lever?

butterfly-valves.guideTitle: How to choose a butterfly valve

Butterfly valves are short, light and quick to open, so they suit water and cooling lines where a gate valve would be heavy. A lock and lever lets you set the disc and hold it in place. A wafer body is clamped between two flanges. Choose the lug type if you need to take off the pipe on one side while the other side stays in service. An S.S disc gives more corrosion resistance than a DI disc.
Match the valve to the flanges it sits between: PN16 and CL150 drilling are not the same at most sizes, so check the mating flange before you order.

DI disc or SS disc?

quick-couplings.h1: QRC, Storz, Bauer and Millar coupling supplier in Dubai
quick-couplings.guideTitle: How to choose a quick coupling
intro: We list QRC (quick-release) couplings, mostly used on compressed air lines. Hose ends and hose plugs come in ¼", 5/16", ⅜" and ½" and in 6, 8, 10 and 12 mm. Male thread couplings, female bodies, female plugs and male plugs come in ¼", ⅜" and ½". Each part is listed in brass and in a carbon steel and stainless version.
We also list Storz couplings from 1½" to 4" in aluminium and stainless steel, plus galvanised Bauer and Millar (Miller) couplings from 3" to 8" for quick hose connections.

Storz couplings are symmetrical: two of the same size lock together with no male or female half, which makes them common on water and pump hoses. Bauer couplings use a ball-and-socket style joint that allows some angle, which helps on long lines laid over uneven ground. Camlock couplings are on our camlock couplings page.

The body is the socket half, which usually stays on the supply side; the plug goes on the equipment or hose. Plugs and bodies must be from the same series to connect, so if you are adding to an existing set, send a photo of the plug you already use. Hose clamps are on our hose clamp page.

Ductile iron universal pipe joining couplings and universal flange adapters, PN10 to PN16, are listed from 2" to 24". A universal coupling joins two plain pipe ends without welding or threading, a common way to repair a damaged section or connect new pipe to old. A universal flange adapter turns a plain pipe end into a flanged end. Measure the actual outside diameter of the pipe before you order, because pipes of the same nominal size can differ by material.

For a quote, WhatsApp the coupling type, size, hose end and the quantity. For a QRC part, say body or plug and brass or steel. For a universal coupling or flange adapter, add the measured outside diameter and the pipe material.
faq: What is the difference between a Storz and a camlock coupling?
A Storz coupling has two identical halves that twist together. A camlock has a male adapter and a female coupler held by cam arms.
Will your QRC plug fit my existing coupling?
Only if they are the same series. Send a photo of your plug or body on WhatsApp and we will check it against our list.
Brass or steel QRC?
Each part is listed in brass and in a carbon steel and stainless version. Send a photo of the part it has to connect to and we confirm which one fits.
Do I need to weld or thread the pipe for a universal coupling?
No. Universal couplings and flange adapters fit onto plain pipe ends.
Do you have rubber washers for these couplings?
Yes. Rubber washers for Chicago, camlock, Storz, Bauer and Miller couplings are listed on our gaskets page.
Which camlock type do I need?
It depends on which half you need and whether it ends in a thread or a hose shank. Our camlock couplings page lists types A to F, DC and DP.

intro: We list G.I flexible connectors in Dubai in two forms. The union type comes from ½" to 3" for screwed pipework. The flanged (F/T) type comes in CL150 and PN16 drilling from 1" to 16".

A flexible connector takes up vibration, small movement and minor misalignment, which is why it goes on pump suction and discharge, chillers and other equipment connections. Use the union type on small screwed lines and the flanged type on larger lines, and match the drilling (CL150 or PN16) to your flanges. Support the pipe on both sides; the connector is not meant to carry pipe weight or fix a large misalignment.
Hammer unions for oilfield lines are on our hammer union page, and universal couplings and flange adapters are on our couplings page.
For a quote, WhatsApp the size, union or flanged, CL150 or PN16, and the quantity.
faq: CL150 or PN16 flexible connector?
Match the drilling of the flanges it bolts to. Our flanged G.I flexible connector is listed in both.
Can a flexible connector correct a large misalignment?
No. It takes vibration and small movement. Correct a large misalignment in the pipework first.

intro: We supply hammer unions for high-pressure oilfield lines: wing-nut hammer unions, blanking unions and hose connectors. They are sold from our counter in Al Quoz Industrial Area 3, with delivery anywhere in the UAE for orders from AED 5,000.

A hammer union joins two pipe ends with a threaded wing nut that you tighten with a hammer, so lines can be made up and broken quickly on site. A blanking union closes off an open end. Hammer unions are made in figure numbers, and the figure sets the design and pressure class. Different figures do not connect to each other, so always order by figure number and size, never by size alone.

For a quote, WhatsApp the figure number, size, end type (threaded or butt-weld), whether you need the male half, female half or the complete union, and the quantity. A photo of the markings on the nut helps.
faq: Which figure numbers do you supply?

Can two different figures be joined?
No. Different figures have different threads and seals. Both halves must be the same figure and size.

Class 150, PN16 and JIS 10K drilling do not match at most sizes, so check the standard on the mating flange; our flange chart lists Class 150 and Class 300 dimensions. For a quote, WhatsApp the size, flange type, class, PN or K, material and quantity, plus the pipe schedule for weld neck.
faq: CL150 or PN16 flange?

CL150 is the ASME class and PN16 the EN pressure number. Their bolt patterns differ at most sizes, so match the flange to what it bolts to. Our flange chart shows the Class 150 and Class 300 dimensions.
SORF or WNRF?
SORF slips over the pipe and suits general service. WNRF is butt-welded to the pipe and is the choice for higher pressure or temperature.

Long radius (LR) elbows have a centre-to-face of 1.5 times the pipe size and give a smoother flow. Short radius (SR) elbows, at 1 times, save space. Use an eccentric reducer on pump suction, flat side up, so air does not collect. Match the fitting schedule to the pipe wall so the bores line up for welding.
For a quote, WhatsApp the fitting, size, schedule, grade (304 or 316) and the quantity.
faq: LR or SR elbow?
Choose LR for most lines. Use SR only where space is tight. Our S.S elbows are listed in both.
Concentric or eccentric reducer?
Concentric keeps the centre line and suits vertical runs. Eccentric keeps one side flat and is used on pump suction and pipe racks.

Socket weld fittings suit small-bore lines at higher pressure, where a threaded joint could leak and a butt weld is hard to make. Push the pipe into the socket, then pull it back about 1.6 mm before welding to leave an expansion gap. Pick the class to match the pipe: CL3000 is usually paired with SCH80 pipe, CL6000 with SCH160 and CL9000 with XXS.
For stainless lines, S.S threaded fittings are on our stainless steel page, and forged C.S threaded fittings are on our threaded forged fittings page.

faq: Match the class to the pipe wall. CL3000 is normally used with SCH80 pipe, CL6000 with SCH160 and CL9000 with XXS.
Why leave a gap before welding?
The gap of about 1.6 mm lets the pipe expand as the weld cools, which helps stop the weld cracking.
Socket weld or threaded?
Socket weld gives a stronger joint that is less likely to leak. Threaded fittings are easier to take apart; our threaded forged fittings page lists the C.S threaded range.

NPT or BSPT?

intro: We list foot valves for pump suction lines: brass foot valves, BSPT, from ½" to 4", including a net type in brass and SS; cast iron foot valves, flanged PN16 with leather flap from 4" to 8" or NPT with rubber flap from 2" to 8"; and PVC foot valves, NPT, from 1" to 6". A foot valve sits at the bottom end of a pump suction pipe. Its strainer keeps out debris and its non-return action holds water in the pipe so the pump stays primed. Size it to the suction pipe, not the pump outlet, and keep it clear of the tank or sump floor so mud is not drawn in. A float valve shuts the inlet when a tank fills.

faq: What does a foot valve do?
It stops water draining back out of the suction pipe, so the pump stays primed, and its strainer keeps debris out.

_pages.title: NPT vs BSPT Threads: How to Tell Them Apart | Fakhri Tools
_pages.desc: NPT and BSPT look alike but do not seal reliably together. Thread angle, threads per inch by size and a quick check before you buy fittings in the UAE.
_pages.h1: NPT vs BSPT: how to tell the two pipe threads apart
_pages.lead: NPT and BSPT are both tapered pipe threads, and both are common on UAE sites. They look alike, but they have a different thread angle and, at most sizes, a different number of threads per inch.

list: Thread angle: NPT is 60°, BSPT is 55°.
Threads per inch (TPI): different at most sizes, the same at ½" and ¾".

table.caption: NPT vs BSPT threads per inch
head: Size
NPT (TPI)
BSPT (TPI)

sections.h2: A simple way to tell them apart
p: Use a thread pitch gauge. At ⅛", ¼", ⅜" and 1" to 2", count the threads per inch: the gauge that sits cleanly in the thread tells you NPT or BSPT straight away.
At ½" and ¾", both threads have 14 TPI, so counting will not help. Check the thread angle instead with a 55° and a 60° gauge: the one that fits the thread profile with no gap is the answer.
If you have no gauge, bring the part or a fitting that screws onto it to our counter and we will check it with you.

sections.h2: Why you should not mix them
p: At ½" and ¾" an NPT part may screw a few turns into a BSPT part, because the pitch is the same. The thread angles still differ, so the flanks do not seal and the joint can leak under pressure. Do not rely on extra tape or sealant to make a mixed joint hold. Match the thread instead.

Many of our items are listed in both: brass and SS ball and gate valves, SS Y-strainers, GI fittings (BSP or NPT), camlocks and GI king nipples. Tell us which thread you need on WhatsApp, and for pipe threading at the counter, tell us the thread type before you come.

faq: Can NPT and BSPT fittings be screwed together?
At ½" and ¾" they may engage a few turns, but they do not seal reliably. Use matching threads.
How do I check a ½" thread?
Use a 55° and a 60° thread gauge, because both NPT and BSPT have 14 TPI at that size.
Do you sell fittings in both threads?
Yes. Many of our valves and fittings are listed in NPT and BSPT. Tell us which one you need when you send your list.

_pages.title: Valve Types and Uses: Gate, Globe, Ball, Check | Fakhri
_pages.desc: When to use a gate, globe, ball, check or butterfly valve or a Y-strainer, and which body, class and end connection fits your line. A short buyer guide.
_pages.h1: Types of valves and their uses: a short buyer guide
_pages.lead: The right valve type for the job saves trouble later. This guide covers the five valve types and the Y-strainer you will meet on most sites, and what each one is for.

table.caption: Which valve for which job
head: Type
Use it for
Avoid it for
rows: On/off isolation, fully open or fully closed
Lines where pressure drop must be low
Isolation; it cannot be closed by hand
Lines that need a full, clear bore
Catching debris before pumps, meters and valves
Shutting off flow; it is not a valve

p: A gate valve lifts a wedge clear of the flow, so when it is fully open the bore is almost unobstructed. Use it for isolation. Left part-open, the wedge vibrates and the seats wear.
A globe valve turns the flow through the body past a plug and seat, which makes it good at regulating flow. The trade-off is a higher pressure drop than a gate or ball valve.

A quarter turn opens or closes a ball valve, so it is fast and easy to see whether it is open. 1PC bodies are compact, 2PC bodies are general purpose, and 3PC bodies can be serviced in the line. A 3-way ball valve diverts flow.

A check valve opens with forward flow and closes when flow reverses. Swing types suit horizontal lines; spring and vertical types can work in vertical lines with upward flow; wafer and dual-disk types are short and fit between flanges, such as after a pump.

A butterfly valve turns a disc in the bore. It is short and light, which suits large water and cooling lines. Use a lever on smaller sizes and a gear operator on larger ones. A lug body lets you remove the pipe on one side.
A Y-strainer holds a screen in a side leg to catch scale and debris. Fit it upstream of the item you want to protect, with the leg pointing down on horizontal lines.

list: Body: CS (WCB or forged A105) for oil, gas and process lines; SS (CF8, CF8M, 316L) for corrosive or clean service; CI, brass or bronze for water.
Class: match the valve to the line, for example CL150, CL300, PN16 or 800 WOG.
Ends: flanged for larger lines, NPT, BSPT or SW for small bore. Match the thread to the pipe.

faq: Can I throttle with a ball valve?
Only briefly. Long-term throttling wears the seats. Use a globe valve to regulate flow.
Do I need a Y-strainer before a pump?
It is good practice. A strainer upstream stops scale and weld slag reaching the pump.
Which valve should go after a pump?
Usually a check valve to stop back-flow, plus an isolation valve such as a gate, ball or butterfly valve.

_pages.desc: ASME B16.5 Class 150 and 300 flange OD, bolt circle and bolts in mm, ½" to 24", and why Class 150, PN16 and JIS 10K flanges do not swap.
_pages.h1: Flange chart: Class 150 and Class 300 dimensions, and PN16 vs JIS 10K
_pages.lead: Outside diameter, bolt circle (PCD), number of bolts and bolt size for ASME B16.5 Class 150 and Class 300 flanges from ½" to 24", with a plain guide to why Class 150, PN16 and JIS 10K flanges are not the same.

p: NPS is the nominal pipe size. The flange OD is the outside diameter of the flange plate. The bolt circle, or PCD (pitch circle diameter), is the circle through the centres of the bolt holes. Two flanges bolt together only when the PCD, the number of bolts and the bolt size all match.

For the same pipe size, a Class 300 flange is larger than a Class 150 flange and usually has more or bigger bolts, so the two classes do not bolt together. Weld neck, slip-on, socket weld, threaded and blind flanges of the same class and size share the same OD and drilling.

p: These are three different flange systems. Class 150 comes from the American standard ASME B16.5 and is drilled in inch dimensions. PN16 comes from the European standard EN 1092-1 and is drilled in metric dimensions with metric bolts. JIS 10K comes from the Japanese standard JIS B2220 and has its own metric drilling.

Although the pressure ratings sound similar, the OD, the bolt circle, the bolt count and the bolt size differ at most sizes. In general a Class 150 flange will not bolt to a PN16 or a JIS 10K flange, and a PN16 flange will not bolt to a JIS 10K flange. Even where a bolt circle comes close, the holes or the bolts may not line up properly, so do not force a mixed joint.

Valves, pumps and equipment from different countries often arrive with different flanges. Before you order, check the marking on the mating flange or the drawing, or measure the OD, the PCD and the bolt holes and send them to us.

faq: Will a Class 150 flange bolt to a PN16 flange?
Not in general. The bolt circle, the number of bolts and the bolt size differ at most sizes. Check the standard on the mating flange and order the same one.
How do I identify a flange I already have?

Read the marking stamped on the rim, which usually shows the size, the class, PN or K, and the material. If there is no marking, measure the OD, the bolt circle (PCD), the number of holes and the hole size, and send them on WhatsApp.
Do Class 150 and Class 300 flanges share the same drilling?
No. A Class 300 flange of the same size has a larger OD and bolt circle, and often more or bigger bolts.
